Marcus — quick tech note from Platform Ops: Zip's validator is aggressive about incremental updates and certain embedded XMP namespaces. When DocuSign completes a PDF it often leaves an incremental update (to preserve the signature object) which some vendor portals then strip during their storage/virus-scan step, resulting in a file that appears unsigned.

Workarounds/options:
1) Vendor-side: Print-to-PDF or use Adobe “Flatten” / “Save as Optimized PDF” to remove incremental updates before upload. (This is what Angela observed.)
2) Redwood-side: We can accept the DocuSign envelope (envelope id + completed PDF) and run our internal PDF sanitizer that flattens signatures and re-uploads a portal-compatible copy. That requires vendor permission and a signed data-handling acknowledgment.
3) Temporary: Ask vendor to use Coupa upload (their portal accepted the DocuSign copy in testing) or email the completed PDF to procurement@redwood.com and we’ll do manual ingestion.

Ive attached short steps for flattening on Windows/macOS and a sample command-line using qpdf. If you want Platform Ops to do the sanitize + re-upload, we need: envelope id (if DocuSign), completed PDF, and vendor sign-off for us to touch/ingest the file.

Hi Angela,

Thanks for the screenshot and for testing. Two practical paths:

1) Quick vendor-side fix (recommended if you prefer no data exchange): Open the completed DocuSign PDF and “Print to PDF” (macOS: File > Print > PDF > Save as PDF; Windows: Print > Microsoft Print to PDF). Then upload that flattened PDF to the Zip portal. We found this removes the incremental signature object and Zip accepts the file.

2) If you want Redwood to handle it: reply with the DocuSign envelope id or send the completed PDF to procurement@redwood.com and well sanitize it for portal ingestion. To proceed with option 2 we need the vendor's explicit permission to process the file and a one-line email stating consent. We will: receive the completed PDF, run a PDF sanitizer to flatten the signature, and upload the sanitized copy to Zip on your behalf. We will not retime or alter any signed fields beyond removing incremental structure.

If neither option works, you can also upload to Coupa (we confirmed Coupa accepts the DocuSign copy) and we will link the supplier account manually.

Please confirm which option you prefer and attach the DocuSign envelope id if you want Redwood to ingest it.
